candidates.title: Magnetic texture-depth break
candidates.layers: Raw competition RTP band 2; gravity band 13 and existing terrain in matched control
candidates.signature: Fixed sigma 1/3 high-pass, 5x5 RMS; opposite-side texture contrast at ±2/±5 pixels, repeated ±5 pixels along strike
candidates.mechanism: Fault-related sudden burial-depth change of magnetic volcanic bedrock suppresses short wavelengths on one side; a covered strand may lack a strong scarp
candidates.difference: Side-specific spectral roughness, not gradient/worm amplitude, multiscale direction agreement or signed amplitude steps
candidates.confounders: Depositional/volcanic contacts, magnetic boulders, terrain clearance and leveling/gridding seams

candidates.reason: No original clean H19 comparator or separately locked complete fresh fit/control protocol; 40/100m cells do not verify 200/400m-flight-line texture resolution

candidates.title: Positive gravity cementation ridge
candidates.layers: Raw isostatic gravity band 13, RTP band 2 and low-relief terrain
candidates.signature: Positive central residual with negative flanks at fixed 300/600m baselines and line coherence
candidates.mechanism: Silica/carbonate cementation could increase alluvial density along a former fluid pathway and expose a covered mineralized strand
candidates.difference: Positive central ridge, not a monotone basin-margin step, magnitude-only worm or demagnetization product
candidates.confounders: Dense shallow bedrock/volcanics, nonhydrothermal soil carbonate, station/interpolation artifacts; cementation can seal permeability
candidates.reason: Regional gridding cannot be assumed to resolve the 1976 road-profile 150–300m anomalies; no field transform or score

candidates.title: Paired opposing scarps and trough
candidates.layers: Raw USGS 3DEP 10m terrain, exactly aggregated to competition grid
candidates.signature: Two parallel breaks 200–800m apart, opposite slope polarity and enclosed low after removing a local plane; label-free proposals
candidates.mechanism: Synthetic/antithetic fault strands enclose a structural trough; weak secondary strands may evade regional mapping
candidates.difference: Explicit breakline pairing and trough geometry instead of individual antislope/openness/scarp maxima
candidates.confounders: Channels, beach ridges, glacial morphology, mass wasting, roads and folding
candidates.status: DEFERRED / RAW TILE AND AGGREGATION COVERAGE UNVERIFIED
candidates.reason: Pinned terrain derivatives are not raw paired-breakline geometry; raw tile obtainability/coverage must be verified before viability
